skill.name: list-hygiene-monitor
skill.description: Monitor email list health through engagement cohorts, bounce trends, complaint trends, and suppression drift. Build measured re-permission, sunset, and prune worklists.
skill.summary: Track list decay and produce evidence-based subscriber hygiene worklists.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting and relative documentation links. One instruction executes bundled Python connector commands against live email data, and saved worklists may retain sensitive subscriber information.

remediation.issue: The Resend measurement workflow invokes local connector and ledger commands.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before execution, validate list identifiers, quote every argument, and document the connector data scope.

remediation.issue: Saved hygiene worklists may retain subscriber addresses and engagement history.
remediation.suggestion: Minimize subscriber fields, redact reports when possible, restrict access, and define retention and deletion rules for saved results.

content.user_title: Monitor Email List Health and Decay
content.value_statement: Aging lists can weaken engagement and sender reputation without clear warning. This skill measures decay and creates prioritized hygiene worklists.
actual_capabilities: Groups subscribers into active, cooling, dormant, deep-dormant, and never-engaged cohorts.
Compares hard-bounce and spam-complaint rates with benchmarks and prior baselines.
Checks suppression-list growth and identifies possible opt-out leakage.
Builds measured re-permission, sunset, and prune worklists.
Marks SEND list-hygiene and engagement-decay sub-items from available evidence.
Defines the next monitoring cadence and baseline comparison.
limitations: Requires ESP exports or connector access for measured subscriber data.
Cannot calculate trend deltas without a prior baseline.
Does not run authentication checks or calculate a full email quality score.
Does not own consent records or automatically execute campaigns.

use_cases.title: Review a Growing Newsletter
use_cases.description: Measure inactive cohorts and prepare a quarterly sunset worklist before engagement declines further.

use_cases.title: Investigate Deliverability Drift
use_cases.description: Compare bounce and complaint rates with the previous campaign cycle and flag worsening trends.

use_cases.title: Plan Subscriber Re-permission
use_cases.description: Separate eligible dormant subscribers from bounced, complained, and suppressed addresses before a win-back campaign.

prompt_templates.title: Basic List Health Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this ESP export. Group subscribers by engagement recency and summarize the main list-health concerns.
prompt_templates.scenario: First review with one current export

prompt_templates.title: Build a Hygiene Worklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this list and create sized re-permission, sunset, and prune groups. Label every count as measured or estimated.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Health Trends
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare current bounce, complaint, and engagement data with this baseline. Report numeric changes and identify suppression drift.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Full Hygiene Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this newsletter list, baseline, and suppression history. Produce cohorts, risk trends, action groups, SEND readings, and the next review cadence.

output_examples.input: A newsletter export contains 20,000 subscribers, including 4,000 inactive for more than 180 days.
output_examples.output: Deep-dormant load is 20 percent. Prepare one re-permission attempt, then sunset nonresponders from active sends.

output_examples.input: Complaint rate rose from 0.06 percent to 0.14 percent while 120 suppressed addresses remain active.
output: Complaint trend increased by 0.08 percentage points and crossed the watch threshold.
Hold the next send for auditor review and prune leaked addresses.

output_examples.input: Current bounce data is available, but no previous hygiene report was provided.
output_examples.output: Report the current bounce rate only. Mark the trend as needs input and use this run as the next baseline.

best_practices: Provide current ESP data, a prior baseline, and suppression history for each review.
Label measured values and estimates clearly in every cohort and trend.
Confirm storage before saving subscriber worklists or hygiene summaries.
anti_patterns: Do not invent trend changes when no prior baseline exists.
Do not re-permission subscribers who bounced, complained, or opted out.
Do not treat this skill as an authentication audit or final quality gate.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide engagement recency, bounce and complaint data, suppression history, the list profile, and an earlier baseline when available.

faq.question: Can it work without subscriber-level records?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use cohort rates, but results must be labeled estimated rather than measured.

faq.question: Does it send re-permission campaigns?
faq.answer: No. It prepares the eligible worklist and hands campaign execution to a separate workflow.

faq.question: Can it calculate a full email quality score?
faq.answer: No. It supplies list-hygiene and engagement-decay evidence for a separate auditor.

faq.question: How often should monitoring run?
faq.answer: Use monthly reviews for frequent promotional sends and quarterly reviews for newsletters or retention programs.

faq.question: How are saved results handled?
faq.answer: The skill asks before saving. Stored reports should minimize subscriber data and follow access and retention controls.
